text:
Jamie Oleksiak signed in Vancouver on July 1 to be a steadying veteran on a rebuilding team, and the steadiness is being tested. The Canucks have lost the last eight games he has played. The 6-foot-7 defenseman, 33, has still been one of the more productive pieces on the blue line, with seven points in 19 games after 15 in 78 last season with Seattle.

Our numbers split his season in two. His own scoring is running hot: two goals on 0.62 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and a scoring rate above the top of our range for him. But the team around him has been unlucky. Vancouver has scored 8.1 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that usually swings back. The process is better than the record suggests too: the Canucks' share of expected goals at five on five is six points higher with him on than off. His defending at the line is real, with Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking showing him stopping 18% of entries aimed at him last season (typical is 11%). The weak spot is getting out of his own end with control.
headline: Jamie Oleksiak is better than Vancouver's losing streak
